classification.difficultyReason: Follow the supplied strip construction and height-finding instruction, substitute into the parabola equation and sum the resulting triangle and trapezium areas.

content.prompt:
Below is the graph of a parabola with equation $y=\frac14x^2$, plotted over the interval $x=-3$ to $x=3$. Estimate the area between the parabola and the $x$-axis by finding the area of four trapezia and two triangles that approximate this region, as shown.

Note: First find the height of each of the vertical lines drawn below.

spec.description: Equation-driven parabola and straight sampled joins at every integer from -3 to 3. Four trapezia and two triangles remain distinct through internal vertical boundaries and alternating light blue fill. The source has no y-scale, grid, axis arrows or axis titles.
spec.mathematics: y=x^2/4 on [-3,3]; sampled heights 9/4,1,1/4,0,1/4,1,9/4. These derived heights are used geometrically without printing answer labels.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source x-axis labels are visible; sampled heights and areas are withheld.

answer.short:
$\dfrac{19}{4}$ square units.

Add the four unit-width trapezia and two triangles using heights from $y=\frac14x^2$.
answer.worked:
The heights at $x=-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3$ are $\frac94,1,\frac14,0,\frac14,1,\frac94$, respectively. Each strip has width $1$. By symmetry, calculate the three strips on one side and double.

$$\begin{align*} A_{\text{triangle}}&=\frac12(1)\left(\frac14\right)=\frac18,\\ A_{\text{inner trapezium}}&=\frac12(1)\left(\frac14+1\right)=\frac58,\\ A_{\text{outer trapezium}}&=\frac12(1)\left(1+\frac94\right)=\frac{13}{8},\\ A_{\text{estimate}}&=2\left(\frac18+\frac58+\frac{13}{8}\right),\\ A_{\text{estimate}}&=\frac{19}{4}\text{ square units}. \end{align*}$$
